lessons.title: The DevOps map
lessons.scope: What DevOps is (culture, practices, tools; dev and ops sharing ownership of running software). The path of one code change from laptop to users: code, build, test, package, release, deploy, run, observe, feedback. Where each tool in this course sits: Docker packages, GitHub Actions automates, Terraform creates infrastructure, Kubernetes runs, Argo CD deploys from git, Prometheus/Grafana/OpenTelemetry observe. Core ideas: automate everything repeatable, everything as code, small frequent changes, fast feedback. DORA metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change fail rate, time to restore). Roles: DevOps engineer, SRE, platform engineer. How this course works (daily rhythm, the hello-devops project you ship all course). No installs today.

lessons.title: Set up your laptop
lessons.scope: Mac (Apple Silicon) first, with short Windows (WSL2) and Linux notes. Install and verify with a version command each: Homebrew, git, a GitHub account with gh auth login, VS Code plus extensions (Docker, YAML, HashiCorp Terraform, Kubernetes), Docker Desktop (mention OrbStack and Colima as alternatives), kubectl, kind, helm, terraform (HashiCorp tap, since homebrew-core froze it), optional k9s and jq. Create the hello-devops repo with the starter files (app.py, requirements.txt, requirements-dev.txt, test_app.py, .gitignore) given in full in `code`, run it in a Python venv, run pytest, push the first commit with gh repo create. Troubleshooting table as bullets. This lesson may run 40 to 50 minutes.

lessons.title: The terminal and Linux you need
lessons.scope: Why Linux matters (servers and containers run Linux). Shell basics: pwd, ls -la, cd, mkdir -p, cp, mv, rm, cat, less, head, tail -f. Absolute vs relative paths, home (~). Permissions (rwx, chmod, chown, sudo, root and why containers should not run as root). Processes (ps, top, kill; SIGTERM vs SIGKILL, which is what docker stop and Kubernetes do). Environment variables (export, $PATH, env). Pipes and redirection (|, >, >>, 2>&1, grep, wc). Exit codes ($? and why CI fails on non-zero). Package managers (apt, brew). SSH and keys in brief. A tiny bash script with set -euo pipefail.

lessons.title: Networks and the cloud, explained simply
lessons.scope: IP addresses (public vs private, 127.0.0.1 localhost, what binding to 0.0.0.0 means and why apps in containers must do it). Ports. DNS (names to IPs, dig or nslookup). HTTP request and response, status codes, curl -v. TLS and HTTPS certificates in brief. Load balancers and reverse proxies. Firewalls and security groups. The cloud: renting computers by the minute; regions and availability zones; IaaS, PaaS, SaaS, serverless; the big three and the name map (EC2 / Azure VM / Compute Engine; S3 / Blob Storage / Cloud Storage); VPC and subnets at a high level; shared responsibility; pay-as-you-go cost traps and how to avoid bill shock (budgets and alerts, destroy what you create).

lessons.title: Containers: your first docker run
lessons.scope: The 'works on my machine' problem. VM vs container (shared kernel; namespaces and cgroups in one plain sentence each). Image vs container (class vs object). Registries (Docker Hub). docker run with -d, -p, --name, -e, --rm; docker ps, logs, exec, stop, rm, images, pull. Port mapping explained (host port to container port). Run nginx and redis. Container lifecycle. Docker Desktop on a Mac runs a small Linux VM. arm64 vs amd64 in one short note.

lessons.title: Dockerfiles: package your own app
lessons.scope: Dockerfile instructions: FROM, WORKDIR, COPY, RUN, ENV, ARG, EXPOSE, CMD vs ENTRYPOINT. Build context and .dockerignore. Layers and the build cache (copy requirements.txt before the code so installs are cached). Tags and versions (do not rely on latest). Build and run hello-devops with a simple single-stage Dockerfile (port 8000, gunicorn). docker history and docker inspect. Config through environment variables (the twelve-factor idea in one paragraph).

lessons.title: Data, networks and Docker Compose
lessons.scope: Containers are disposable, so where does data go: volumes vs bind mounts. Container networking: user-defined bridge networks, DNS by container name. Docker Compose: compose.yaml with services, build, image, ports, environment, volumes, depends_on with a healthcheck condition. docker compose up -d, ps, logs -f, exec, down, down -v. Add Redis to hello-devops so the visit counter survives restarts (REDIS_HOST=redis). .env files for Compose. The lab's compose.yaml is the target.

lessons.title: Production-ready images and registries
lessons.scope: Multi-stage builds. Base image trade-offs (slim, alpine, distroless, Docker Hardened Images if research confirms). Run as non-root (USER). HEALTHCHECK. Measuring image size. Scanning images (docker scout and trivy). Tags vs digests (immutable). Pushing to a registry: Docker Hub and GHCR (docker login, docker tag, docker push). Multi-arch builds with docker buildx --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 (Mac arm64 vs cloud amd64). Never bake secrets into images. Ends with the lab's final Dockerfile (multi-stage, venv, ARG APP_VERSION, non-root uid 10001).

lessons.title: Git, pull requests and CI/CD ideas
lessons.scope: Git for teams: commit, branch, merge, pull request, code review, merge conflicts in brief. Trunk-based development vs GitFlow. What CI is. What CD is (continuous delivery vs continuous deployment). Pipeline stages. Build once, deploy many. Deployment strategies overview: rolling, blue/green, canary, feature flags. Semantic versioning and git tags. Hands-on: feature branch and a pull request on hello-devops using gh.

lessons.title: GitHub Actions: your first workflow
lessons.scope: Anatomy: a YAML file in .github/workflows; events (push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch, schedule); jobs; steps; runners (GitHub-hosted vs self-hosted); uses: (actions) vs run: (shell). The Actions tab and reading logs. Contexts and expressions (${{ github.sha }}, ${{ github.ref_name }}). env at workflow, job and step level. Billing in one line (free minutes for public repos; check current limits). Hands-on: a hello workflow, then run pytest on every push.

lessons.title: A real CI pipeline: test, lint, cache, matrix
lessons.scope: Build the lab's ci.yml step by step: setup-python with pip cache, ruff and pytest, a matrix across Python 3.13 and 3.14, needs: for job order, a docker build check job, upload-artifact for test reports. Branch protection or rulesets with required status checks so broken code cannot merge. concurrency to cancel stale runs, paths filters, timeout-minutes. Making CI fast. Running workflows locally with act (mention).

lessons.title: Ship it: build and push images safely
lessons.scope: Secrets and variables (repository and environment level), never echo secrets. GITHUB_TOKEN and the permissions block (least privilege). Build and push to GHCR on a version tag with docker/login-action, docker/metadata-action and docker/build-push-action (the lab's release.yml). Environments with required reviewers as an approval gate. OIDC to the cloud instead of long-lived keys (concept plus the aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials snippet). Reusable workflows and composite actions. Supply-chain hygiene: pin third-party actions to a full commit SHA, Dependabot for actions, the danger of pull_request_target with untrusted code.

lessons.title: Infrastructure as Code and your first Terraform
lessons.scope: Why IaC (the problems of clicking in consoles: drift, no review, no repeatability). Declarative vs imperative. Terraform vs OpenTofu (the 2023 licence change and the Linux Foundation fork; commands are nearly identical). Where Pulumi, CloudFormation and Ansible fit. HCL basics: blocks, arguments, references. Providers and resources. The workflow: init, plan, apply, destroy; reading a plan (+, ~, -/+, -). Hands-on with the kreuzwerker/docker provider: run an nginx container from Terraform on your laptop, change it, destroy it. No cloud account needed.

lessons.title: Variables, state and modules
lessons.scope: Input variables (types, defaults, descriptions, terraform.tfvars, -var), outputs, locals, data sources. References and the dependency graph (terraform graph). State: what terraform.tfstate holds, why it matters, never edit it by hand, it can contain secrets; remote backends with locking (S3 backend with use_lockfile, HCP Terraform). Drift and terraform plan -refresh-only. import blocks. Modules: root vs child, using a registry module, writing a small module. count vs for_each in brief. lifecycle (prevent_destroy, create_before_destroy). Hands-on: the lab's infra/local (app + Redis + network with variables and outputs).

lessons.title: Terraform on a real cloud, and in CI
lessons.scope: Optional cloud part with clear cost warnings: AWS account safety first (root MFA, do not use root, IAM Identity Center or an IAM user, a budget alert). Provider auth (aws configure sso or env vars). Create a private, versioned S3 bucket with Terraform, then move state to an S3 backend, then destroy. Check the current AWS free tier rules in research. Terraform in GitHub Actions: fmt, validate and plan on pull requests; apply on merge to main behind an environment approval; auth with OIDC (an IAM role trusting token.actions.githubusercontent.com). Linters and scanners: tflint, trivy config or checkov. Writes the lab's infra/aws and .github/workflows/terraform.yml.

lessons.title: Why Kubernetes, and how a cluster works
lessons.scope: The problems at scale: many containers on many machines (placement, restarts, scaling, rollouts, finding each other). Desired state and control loops (reconciliation). Architecture: control plane (API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager) and worker nodes (kubelet, kube-proxy, container runtime such as containerd). Pods as the smallest unit. YAML manifest anatomy (apiVersion, kind, metadata, spec). kubectl get, describe, logs, apply -f, delete, explain. Managed Kubernetes (EKS, AKS, GKE) and when you do NOT need Kubernetes. Hands-on: kind create cluster with the lab's kind-config.yaml, kind load docker-image hello-devops:1.0.0, run a first Pod, port-forward to it.

lessons.title: Deployments and Services
lessons.scope: ReplicaSets and Deployments. Self-healing (delete a pod and watch it come back). Scaling. Rolling updates and rollback (kubectl rollout status, history, undo; kubectl set image; maxSurge and maxUnavailable). Labels and selectors. Services: ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, headless in one line. Cluster DNS (service.namespace.svc.cluster.local). kubectl port-forward. Namespaces. Hands-on: the lab's k8s/namespace.yaml, deployment.yaml and service.yaml; curl several times and watch the host field change across pods; roll from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0 and back.

lessons.title: Config, secrets, health checks and scaling
lessons.scope: ConfigMaps (env, envFrom, mounted files). Secrets (base64 is not encryption; mention External Secrets Operator and Sealed Secrets; enable encryption at rest in managed clusters). Probes: liveness, readiness, startup, using the app's /healthz and /readyz. Resources: requests vs limits, OOMKilled, CPU throttling. HorizontalPodAutoscaler (needs metrics-server; on kind it needs the --kubelet-insecure-tls flag). Debugging: CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, Pending, kubectl describe, kubectl get events, kubectl logs --previous. Hands-on: the lab's configmap.yaml, redis.yaml, probes in deployment.yaml and hpa.yaml; break Redis and watch readiness pull pods out of the Service.

lessons.title: Ingress, Gateway API, storage and Helm
lessons.scope: Getting outside traffic in: Ingress vs the Gateway API (the newer standard; research the current state of ingress-nginx, which announced its retirement). Install one Gateway API controller on kind and route to hello-devops with an HTTPRoute (verify install commands from official docs). Storage: PersistentVolume, PersistentVolumeClaim, StorageClass; StatefulSet for databases and why managed databases are often the better choice. Helm: charts, values, releases; install a public chart; helm create our own chart; helm upgrade, rollback, template, lint. Kustomize overlays (dev vs prod) as the alternative. Writes the lab's chart/hello-devops.

lessons.title: GitOps with Argo CD
lessons.scope: GitOps principles (OpenGitOps: declarative, versioned and immutable, pulled automatically, continuously reconciled). Push-based vs pull-based deploys. Argo CD architecture in brief. Install Argo CD on kind (verify the current install command), log in to the UI. An Application pointing at the k8s/ folder of your GitHub repo; sync, automated sync, self-heal and prune; drift demo with kubectl scale or kubectl edit; rollback with git revert. How CI updates the image tag in git (kustomize edit set image, or Argo CD Image Updater). Flux as the main alternative. ApplicationSets and app-of-apps in one paragraph. Writes the lab's argocd/application.yaml.

lessons.title: Observability: metrics, logs and traces
lessons.scope: Monitoring vs observability. The signals: metrics, logs, traces (and profiles). Prometheus: pull model, counters, gauges, histograms, labels, PromQL basics such as rate(hello_requests_total[5m]). Grafana dashboards. Install kube-prometheus-stack with Helm on kind and scrape hello-devops /metrics with a ServiceMonitor (verify CRD fields). Logs: write to stdout, collect with an agent, store in Loki or similar. Traces and OpenTelemetry (SDKs plus the Collector; vendor neutral). Golden signals and RED. SLIs, SLOs and error budgets. Alert on symptoms users feel. On-call and blameless postmortems in brief.

lessons.title: DevSecOps and the software supply chain
lessons.scope: Shift left, and security as everyone's job. Real supply-chain incidents, only with sources (for example the xz-utils backdoor in 2024 and the tj-actions/changed-files compromise in 2025). SBOMs (syft; SPDX and CycloneDX). Vulnerability scanning (trivy image and trivy config). Secret scanning (GitHub push protection, gitleaks). Signing images with cosign keyless (Sigstore). Provenance and SLSA levels; GitHub artifact attestations. Policy as code at admission time (Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper) with one small policy such as 'no :latest tags' or 'must run as non-root'. Least privilege everywhere. Add scan, SBOM and signing steps to release.yml.

lessons.title: Platform engineering, AI in DevOps, and your capstone
lessons.scope: Platform engineering and internal developer platforms (golden paths, self-service, Backstage). Developer experience. FinOps (cost visibility, tagging, right-sizing, autoscaling, spot instances). AI in DevOps today: AI coding agents that open and review pull requests, AI-assisted incident response, MCP servers that let agents use Kubernetes, Terraform and GitHub, and guardrails (read-only by default, human review of plans, no production admin keys for agents). Other trends worth a line each: eBPF and Cilium, OpenTofu, serverless containers, WebAssembly. Careers and certifications (KCNA, CKAD, CKA, Terraform Associate, AWS Cloud Practitioner, GitHub Actions). The capstone: take hello-devops end to end (git push, CI tests, image to GHCR, signed, Argo CD deploys to kind, Grafana shows it) as a checklist, and what to learn next.
